items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: I didn't know that about Count Basie and the air conditioner and how he became famous because they decided if they booked the Basie band they’d put in air conditioning.

ctx.x: It’s interesting when you listen to the early rock, that as you said before, “Rock Around the Clock” is a swing-blues, right?

It’s the same tempo as Count Basie’s “One O’Clock Jump” and it’s a blues. But they use the word “rock.” The word rock came in, I mean “Rock Around the Christmas Tree,” they used that word, all the pop artists.

When you listen to some of the early Chuck Berry for instance, you almost hear this very interesting conflict because some of the band is still swinging, and Chuck is playing straight eighth notes on his guitar. It’s like adjusting itself.
